stories.headline: Claude Code Shifts to Auto Mode for Pro, Max, and Team Plans
stories.summary: Anthropic is now making auto mode the default setting for new sessions in most Claude Code plans, citing confidence in its capabilities. This change will take effect on August 14th for Pro, Max, and Team plans.

stories.headline: Fastmail Offers EU Data Region for Enhanced User Security
stories.summary: Fastmail has introduced a new EU data region, allowing users to store their data within the European Union for added security and compliance. This move aims to address growing concerns over data sovereignty and protection.

stories.headline: Breaking Free from Shame: The Church's Role in Eating Disorder Recovery
stories.summary: Eating disorders thrive on shame and secrecy, but the church can play a vital role in helping individuals break free from these cycles and find healing. By embracing love and acceptance, the church can provide a safe space for recovery.

stories.headline: Developer's Astrology App Rejection Sparks Retraction and Reflection
stories.summary: A developer's surprise and frustration over an App Store rejection for an astrology app have led to a retraction and a reflection on the importance of app review processes. The incident highlights the need for developers to carefully review their app submissions.

stories.headline: Australia's Unique Species Face Extinction Amid Alarming Loss Rates
stories.summary: Australia is home to some of the world's most unique species, but the country is experiencing an alarming rate of species loss, making it a global hotspot for extinction. Conservation efforts are necessary to protect these species and preserve Australia's natural heritage.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Dominate AI Revenue with 70% Market Share
stories.summary: Two leading AI companies, OpenAI and Anthropic, have cornered a significant 70% of the AI revenue market, leaving other players struggling to compete. This dominance has significant implications for the AI industry and its future development.

stories.headline: Os8088: A Retro Mac-Like OS for IBM PCs
stories.summary: Os8088 is a powerful, Mac-like operating system designed for IBM PCs, offering a unique blend of retro charm and modern functionality. This open-source OS is gaining attention from enthusiasts and developers alike.

stories.headline: Shopify Scales Inventory Reservations with MySQL Replacement
stories.summary: Shopify has successfully replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations, achieving significant scalability improvements. This move showcases the company's commitment to optimizing its infrastructure for growth and performance.

stories.headline: Interactive Map Visualizes Total Solar Eclipse for August 12
stories.summary: An open-source interactive map has been created to visualize the total solar eclipse on August 12, offering a unique perspective on this celestial event. The map features various layers and settings for customization.

stories.headline: Exploring the Wonders of God's Creation in August's Works & Wonders
stories.summary: The latest edition of Works & Wonders features a collection of thought-provoking articles and reflections on God's creation, including topics such as the nature of God and the beauty of the natural world.

stories.headline: Israel Rejects Trump's Gaza Plan, Demands Hamas Disarm
stories.summary: Israel's PM Netanyahu has rejected the US peace plan for Gaza, insisting that the military will not withdraw until Hamas is genuinely disarmed. The move has sparked concerns about the prospects for a lasting peace in the region.

stories.headline: Ukraine Mourns 'Collector of Souls' Killed in Landmine Blast
stories.summary: Oleksiy Yukov, a Ukrainian soldier who spent two decades recovering the bodies of soldiers, including many Russians, was killed in a landmine blast while on a recovery mission. His bravery and selflessness have been hailed as an inspiration to his countrymen.

stories.headline: Dithered QR Codes: A New Twist on an Old Format
stories.summary: A developer has created a new type of QR code that uses dithering to create a visually striking effect, while still maintaining the code's functionality. The technique has sparked interest among designers and developers looking for new ways to use QR codes.

stories.headline: Turning a Phone into a Server: A Novel Approach to Computing
stories.summary: A developer has shown how to turn a smartphone into a fully functional server, using the device's processing power and storage to run a web server. The technique has implications for the future of mobile computing and the Internet of Things.

stories.headline: Goth's Rebel Spirit: A Look Back at a Classic Album
stories.summary: Pitchfork takes a closer look at a classic album that helped define the goth genre, featuring a spirited rebuke to critics who sought to pigeonhole the music. The album's enduring influence can still be felt in the music scene today.

stories.headline: John C. Lilly's Vision for a New Era of Intelligence
stories.summary: In a 1978 lecture, scientist John C. Lilly outlined his vision for a future where humans could merge with machines to achieve a new level of intelligence. His ideas have been influential in the development of artificial intelligence and robotics.

stories.headline: Trump's Iran Dilemma: How to End a War Without Losing Face
stories.summary: President Trump is facing a classic dilemma in Iran, where a prolonged war has become a defining feature of his presidency. The question is how to extricate the US from the conflict without appearing weak or defeated.

stories.headline: Corrupt Minds Think Alike: The FIFA Scandal
stories.summary: A group of FIFA officials were caught up in a corruption scandal, despite the organization's efforts to present a positive image. The incident highlights the deep-seated problems within the organization and the need for reform.

stories.headline: Porting Oberon to RISC-V: A Technical Feat
stories.summary: A developer has successfully ported the Oberon operating system to the RISC-V architecture, demonstrating the flexibility and versatility of the system. The achievement has implications for the development of new computer systems and architectures.

stories.headline: Israel Accused of Weaponizing Archaeology in West Bank
stories.summary: Israel is facing criticism for its plans to expropriate large tracts of land in the West Bank, which could have significant implications for the region's cultural heritage. The move has sparked concerns about the impact on Palestinian communities and the preservation of historical sites.

stories.headline: Houthis Launch Attack on Saudi Oil Facility Amid Regional Tensions
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis have claimed responsibility for an attack on an Aramco oil facility in Saudi Arabia, while Iran has made new demands over the restart of negotiations and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Canada Wildfire Rages Out of Control, Residents Warned to Evacuate
stories.summary: A massive wildfire in British Columbia has spread over 39 square miles, prompting warnings for residents to prepare for the worst as the blaze remains out of control.

stories.headline: Tanker Sailors Remain in Limbo Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
stories.summary: An agreement over the Strait of Hormuz remains elusive, leaving tanker sailors in a state of limbo as they navigate the treacherous waterway.

stories.headline: Airy: A Free Voice Content Creation Platform
stories.summary: Airy is a new platform that allows users to create voice content quickly and easily, with a focus on simplicity and speed.

stories.headline: Hormuz Talks Yield Progress, But Breakthrough Remains Uncertain
stories.summary: Talks between Iran and other nations have made progress towards agreeing a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, but a breakthrough remains unclear.

stories.headline: French Wildfires: Hundreds Arrested, But Who's to Blame?
stories.summary: The French government is trying to attribute blame for the devastating wildfires that swept the country last month, with hundreds arrested in connection with the disaster.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Mass Wedding Scheme Aims to Help Couples in Need
stories.summary: A new scheme in Nigeria is offering mass weddings to couples who cannot afford the significant financial costs associated with marriage.

stories.headline: Kosovo Opposition MP Throws Eggs at Acting PM
stories.summary: A Kosovo opposition MP hurled eggs at the country's acting prime minister during a heated exchange in parliament, prompting a police intervention.

stories.headline: Kashmir's First India Test Cricketer Inspires Millions
stories.summary: Auqib Nabi has become the first cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir to be selected for an India Test match, inspiring millions of fans in the region.

stories.headline: Notorious Crime Boss Returns to Ireland in High-Security Operation
stories.summary: Notorious crime boss Daniel Kinahan has been extradited from Dubai and is being transported to court in a high-security operation.

stories.headline: Birth Control Trends May Not Be the Main Reason for Rising Abortions
stories.summary: The increase in abortions in the US may be linked to various factors beyond the decline in birth control pill usage. Experts suggest a more complex interplay of factors is at play.

stories.headline: Reviving a Four-Year-Old eReader with SSH
stories.summary: A developer has successfully revived a four-year-old eReader using SSH, demonstrating the device's potential for continued use and repurposing. This hack showcases the eReader's capabilities beyond its original intended use.

stories.headline: Solar Eclipse Visible in US Next Week
stories.summary: A solar eclipse will be visible in parts of the US next Wednesday, offering a rare opportunity for stargazers to witness this celestial event. Viewers in affected areas should take necessary precautions to safely observe the eclipse.

stories.headline: CSS: The bomb inside your inbox
Uncovering the Alpha 21264 CPU, a Forgotten RISC Chip
stories.summary: A retro computing enthusiast has shared an in-depth look at the Alpha 21264 CPU, a RISC chip developed in the 1990s for NT systems. This article provides a nostalgic glimpse into the history of computer architecture.

stories.headline: Ex-Minister Charged in Ecuadorian Presidential Candidate's Assassination
stories.summary: Ecuadorian prosecutors have charged a former minister and six others, including a cartel leader, in connection with the murder of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. The investigation has uncovered a complex web of alleged involvement.

stories.headline: Woman and Infant Killed in Boat Capsizing Near Statue of Liberty
stories.summary: A boat capsized near the Statue of Liberty, resulting in the deaths of a woman and her infant, while 12 others were rescued in a large search and rescue operation. The incident is currently under investigation.

stories.headline: Native X64 Port of Microsoft Word 1.1a Released
stories.summary: A developer has released a native X64 port of Microsoft Word 1.1a, a vintage version of the popular word processing software. This release allows users to run the classic software on modern systems.

stories.headline: Accenture Struggles to Contain AI Token Abuse
stories.summary: Leaked audio reveals that consulting giant Accenture is grappling with non-technical employees wasting company funds on AI tokens for trivial tasks. This highlights the challenges of implementing AI responsibly within organizations.

stories.headline: Ancient Roman Shipwreck Discovered Off Sicily Coast
stories.summary: Italian authorities have announced the discovery of an ancient Roman shipwreck off the coast of Sicily, describing it as one of the most significant underwater archaeological finds in recent years. The wreck is expected to provide valuable insights into ancient maritime trade and culture.

stories.headline: Solo Sailor Tackles Arctic Ocean Circumnavigation
stories.summary: Matt Rutherford is attempting a world-first feat by sailing 10,000 nautical miles through treacherous ice floes and gales. He's currently on his boat, speaking with NPR about his incredible journey.

stories.headline: Mathematicians Discover Infinite Magic Hexagons
stories.summary: Researchers have found that magic hexagons can be created in any order, opening up new possibilities in mathematics. This breakthrough has significant implications for the field of geometry and beyond.

stories.headline: Futile Prediction: URL to Disappear in 11 Years
stories.summary: A prediction made in 2011 about the availability of a specific URL has been proven correct, highlighting the fleeting nature of online content. The URL will become inaccessible in just 11 years, a stark reminder of the transience of digital existence.

stories.headline: Renaissance Art Meets African Landscape
stories.summary: Marc Padeu's paintings bring a unique blend of Renaissance themes and African culture to the art world. His work is currently on display in a London gallery, offering a fresh perspective on traditional art forms.

stories.headline: LA Neighbourhood Plagued by Rotting Meat Stench
stories.summary: A devastating fire has left a trail of rotting meat in its wake, causing an unbearable stench to plague a Los Angeles neighbourhood. The community is struggling to cope with the aftermath of the disaster.

stories.headline: Author Confronts Dark Hours in New Memoir
stories.summary: Terry Godier's latest work, 'Mea Culpa – Dark Hours', is a deeply personal exploration of the author's inner struggles. The book offers a candid look at the human experience, tackling themes of vulnerability and resilience.

stories.headline: The Knuckle Cracking Conundrum
stories.summary: A recent article has sparked debate about the health implications of cracking one's knuckles. While some argue it's harmless, others claim it can lead to serious health problems, leaving many wondering what to do.

stories.headline: Perez Hilton Faces Long Recovery After Self-Harm Incident
stories.summary: The US blogger is in a stable condition in hospital after reports of a self-harm incident during a livestream. His family has confirmed that he is receiving treatment and is expected to make a full recovery.
